title: TL-CGAN — Robust ECG Classification
summary: Transfer-learning framework built on conditional GANs to strengthen ECG signal classifiers against adversarial attacks, improving reliability for downstream clinical decision-support systems.

sections.label: Problem
sections.text: ECG classifiers deployed in clinical decision-support systems are vulnerable to small, targeted adversarial perturbations that can flip a prediction without any visible distortion to the signal.

sections.label: Approach
sections.text: TL-CGAN fine-tunes a pretrained ECG classifier against adversarially perturbed inputs generated by a conditional generator, trained jointly with the discriminator to produce realistic, class-consistent perturbations.

sections.label: Key Results
items: Preserves clean-signal accuracy within one point of the unmodified baseline
Substantially closes the accuracy gap under FGSM and PGD attack budgets
More sample-efficient robustness gain than standard adversarial training

sections.label: Impact
items: Reduces risk of adversarially-induced misdiagnosis in deployed ECG classifiers
Provides a reusable fine-tuning recipe applicable to other biomedical signal classifiers
Strengthens the case for adversarial robustness testing in clinical AI pipelines

title: Histopathological Skin Cancer Segmentation
summary: A deep neural network approach to segmenting malignant tissue in histopathological skin cancer images, developed with a multi-institution research team as part of ongoing medical imaging work.

sections.label: Problem
sections.text: Accurate delineation of malignant tissue in histopathological whole-slide images is a prerequisite for reliable computer-assisted skin cancer diagnosis — but manual annotation by pathologists is slow, and different annotators don't always agree on exactly where a boundary falls.

sections.label: Approach
sections.text: A convolutional encoder-decoder segmentation pipeline combined with domain-specific pre-processing to handle the color and staining variability that's typical across histopathology datasets collected from different labs and scanners.

sections.label: Status
sections.text: The manuscript is currently in progress. Preliminary results on held-out slides show segmentation masks that closely track expert annotations, and the collaboration is ongoing to extend the dataset and validate the pipeline across additional clinical sites.

title: IoT Research & Capacity-Building Consortium
